texts.facts: 1. This is an application under Order XI Rule 1(4) of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 ('CPC') [as amended by the Commercial Courts, Commercial Division and Commercial Appellate Division of High Courts Act, 2015 ('Commercial Courts Act')] read with Section 151 CPC, seeking leave to file additional documents within thirty (30) days. 2. The Plaintiff, if it wishes to file additional documents will file the same within thirty (30) days from today, and it shall do so strictly as per the provisions of the Commercial Courts Act and the Delhi High Court (Original Side) Rules, 2018 ('DHC Rules'). 3. For the reasons stated in the application, the same is allowed. The authenticity of the order can be re-verified from Delhi High Court Order Portal by scanning the QR code shown above. The is an application under Section 151 of CPC, seeking exemption from service to the Defendants. 6. In view of the fact that the Plaintiff has sought an ex parte ad-interim injunction along with the appointment of a Local Commissioner, the exemption from effecting service upon the Defendants at this stage is granted. 8. This is an application under Section 12A of the Commercial Courts Act, 2015 read with Section 151 CPC, seeking exemption from instituting pre-litigation mediation. 9. Having regard to the facts that the present suit contemplates urgent interim relief and in light of the judgement of the Supreme Court in Yamini Manohar v. T.K.D. Keerthi1, exemption from the requirement of pre- institution mediation is granted to the Plaintiff. The present suit has been filed for permanent injunction restraining the Defendants from infringement and passing off of Trademark, Copyright and other ancillary reliefs. 12. Let the plaint be registered as a suit. 13. The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 28/11/2025 at 21:14:26 14. The summons shall indicate that the written statement(s) must be filed within thirty (30) days from the date of receipt of the summons. The Defendants shall also file affidavit(s) of admission/denial of the documents filed by the Plaintiff, failing which the written statement(s) shall not be taken on record. 15. The Plaintiff is at liberty to file replication thereto within thirty (30) days after filing of the written statement(s). This is an application filed under Order XXXIX Rules 1 and 2 CPC on behalf of the Plaintiff seeking ex parte ad interim injunction against the Defendants. The Plaintiff, incorporated under the laws of Singapore, is a part of the Danone Group of companies engaged in the business of specialized nutrition market as well as in the dairy and plant-based products market, with an established presence in the market for packaged water, as well. The This is a digitally signed order. The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 28/11/2025 at 21:14:26 Plaintiff works in close collaboration with the medical community, including doctors, health authorities, etc. and its unique product range is designed to give health care professionals the scope to select nutritional options that are accurately targeted to support specific management regimes and to enhance patient recovery. 21.2. The Plaintiff's trademark 'PROTINEX' was originally registered by Dumex Limited and was later acquired by the Pfizer group in 1972, finally being acquired by the Wockhardt Group in 2006 eventually being held by Wockhardt EU Operations (Swiss) AG. In 2012, the Wockhardt EU Operations (Swiss) AG executed a deed of assignment in favour of the Plaintiff, transferring all its intellectual properties, goodwill and ancillary rights on the registered trademark 'PROTINEX' and its associated trade dresses, to the Plaintiff. The details of the relevant trademark registrations and applications, registered in India, are mentioned at paragraph 46 of the plaint. 21.3 . The Plaintiff has also applied for copyright of the unique style, distinctive colour scheme and get up of its 'PROTINEX' labels and has obtained registrations under the Copyright Act, 1957. The details of the copyright registrations are mentioned at paragraph 57 of the Plaint. 21.4. The Plaintiff has been exclusively distributing its products through Nutricia International Private limited under the mark 'PROTINEX' and has garnered tremendous sales. The gross sales and the marketing expenses up till 31st March, 2024 is Rs. 3,058.51 lakhs and Rs. 902.03 lakhs, respectively. The details of the gross sales and marketing expenses from 2022-2024 is mentioned at paragraph 37 of the plaint. texts.arguments: Mr. Krishna, learned counsel for the Plaintiff states that on 24.02.2024 Defendant No. 1 filed its Trademark Application No. 6318832 for the impugned mark 'PROTOEX' on a proposed to be used basis in class 5, which was published in the Trademark Journal number 2157-0 dated 20.05.2024. 23.1 He states that the Plaintiff filed its notice of opposition against the aforementioned Application on 11.09.2024 and the Notice of opposition was served upon Defendant No. 1 on 12.09.2024; however, since Defendant no. 1 failed to file the counter statement within the statutory period ending on 12.11.2024, the said application has been declared as abandoned due to non- prosecution. 23.2 He states that the Plaintiff also issued cease and desist notice on 20.08.2024 followed by a reminder notice dated 23.09.2024 upon the Defendant No. 1, thereby calling upon Defendant No. 1 to stop using the deceptively similar trademark 'PROTOEX' and not launch any products 23.7 He states that the trade dress used by the Defendants on their products sold under the impugned mark is deceptively similar to the packaging used by the Plaintiff for its product under the mark 'PROTEINX' which is solely and exclusively associated with the Plaintiff. He states that the Defendants have positioned the mark, 'PROTOEX' in a slanting manner at the centre of the packaging which is identical to the slant of the This is a digitally signed order. He states that the Defendants have also imitated the placement of the liquid splashing mark on the trade dress/packaging as that of the Plaintiff. He refers to the distinctive packaging adopted by the competitors to show that the Defendant's packaging is however deceptively similar to the Plaintiff's packaging.
